chef_bio.background: 三嶋亭 was founded in 明治6年 (1873) and is one of the oldest sukiyaki houses in Japan; the site is written around the 五代目 (fifth-generation master), who keeps a personal Instagram and a 『五代目の想い ~Taro's Way~』 page. The building keeps a tsubo-niwa courtyard garden, a large tatami banquet room, and a ranma carving of 「鹿と紅葉」 by the late lacquer artist 番浦省吾; the shop says the decorative cherry wood in the rooms dates from the founding. None of this belongs to Tokyo. The company's own アクセス page lists exactly three shops — 本店 (寺町三条下る), 高島屋京都店 (下京区四条通河原町西入ル真町52) and 大丸京都店 (下京区四条通高倉西入ル立売西町79) — plus the sister restaurant 翁樹庵 (中京区麩屋町通三条上る油屋町87). Every one of them is in Kyoto. No Tokyo bio has therefore been written.
chef_bio.philosophy: 霜降りすき焼き京懐石 — marbled sukiyaki in the Kyoto kaiseki idiom, in a house kept much as it was at the founding.
chef_bio.specialty: Table-side sukiyaki of marbled beef; beef kaiseki courses; a retail 精肉 (butcher) counter and bentō.

name: 蕎麦 神山
cuisine: Hidden hand-cut soba house in the back streets of Oku-Shibuya: buckwheat stone-milled every morning and cut behind glass, seiro at lunch for around ¥1,000–2,000, and reservation-only soba-kaiseki courses at ¥5,500 / ¥7,700 / ¥11,000 in the evening, with roughly fifty sake
neighborhood: Kamiyama-chō 10-8 in Oku-Shibuya, a residential lane behind Bunkamura — 684 m from Shinsen (Keiō Inokashira line), about 10–12 min on foot from Shibuya Station
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金 12:00-14:00／17:30-21:30（L.O. 21:00）　土 12:00-20:00　日・祝日 定休　※夜は前日までの予約制・コースのみ（5,500円／7,700円／11,000円、2名様から）／土曜日のみ予約不可・蕎麦無くなり次第閉店
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim of any kind, and wheat is unavoidable. The shop's booking copy says 十割蕎麦を毎朝石臼挽き — juwari, 100% buckwheat in the dough — but juwari is not gluten-free in a Japanese soba shop: the board is dusted with 打ち粉 and the tsuyu is ordinary wheat soy sauce, with no gluten-free tamari named anywhere. The evening courses also carry tempura (reviewers who arrive unbooked report being asked 「天ぷらはないけどいいですか？」, i.e. tempura is a booked-course item), and the 板わさ kamaboko served as a shokuzen plate is a fish cake that usually carries wheat starch. Treat this as a no.
vegan_detail: The tsuyu and the soba-yu service are built on bonito dashi, and the house dish is 牛すじ肉の蕎麦湯抜き — beef tendon simmered three days in soba-boiling water, which means the soba water itself is not neutral here. The course format is a soba-ya kaiseki with fish, egg (甘い卵焼き is a standard shokuzen plate) and meat throughout. There is no vegan set and no plant-based tsuyu.

roles: owner-chef (name not published on any source that could be opened)
chef_bio.background: The shop opened on 1 April 2006 and appears on Tabelog under the earlier name 清山 (Kiyoyama) before becoming 神山, taking the name of the street it stands on. It is a deliberately hard-to-find room: reviewers describe it as 「渋谷の最奥、神泉からもほど近い住宅街の路地にひっそりと佇む」 — a lane in the residential far end of Shibuya near Shinsen — and as a long-standing fixture of the 奥渋 (Oku-Shibuya) scene. Twenty seats over two floors (a basement counter of fourteen plus private rooms, and a first floor of eighteen when both are open; Hot Pepper currently lists twelve seats and first-floor-only service), with two half-private rooms and one six-seat private room, all non-smoking, free Wi-Fi. The buckwheat is domestic and stone-milled on the premises each morning, and the cutting is done behind glass so guests can watch powder become noodle; the water used for the dough and the boil is spring water from Mt Haruna in Gunma. Alongside the soba the kitchen runs a three-day beef-tendon simmer finished in soba-yu, and the cellar holds around fifty sake plus craft beer and a house shōchū blend. The room doubles as a rental photography studio through CFAC (¥10,000/hr stills, ¥15,000/hr video), which is how much of the room description reaches the web. No chef's name is published on any source that could be opened, so none has been invented.
chef_bio.philosophy: A soba house as a quiet room away from Shibuya — 隠れ家 (hideaway) framing, own-milled buckwheat, and soba as the finish to a drinking course rather than a quick lunch.
chef_bio.specialty: せいろ (plain cold soba with tsuyu); 牛すじ肉の蕎麦湯抜き, beef tendon simmered three days in soba-boiling water; reservation-only evening courses at ¥5,500 / ¥7,700 / ¥11,000; about fifty Japanese sake.

anecdotes.text: Turn up in the evening without a booking and the greeting is a negotiation: reviewers report being asked 「予約なしだったので、天ぷらはないけどいいですか？」 — 'you have no reservation, so there's no tempura, is that all right?' — before being seated.
The noodles are cut behind glass and the buckwheat is stone-milled each morning; the shop uses spring water from Mt Haruna for the dough and the boil.
The room is let out as a photo studio when it is not serving — ¥10,000 an hour for stills, ¥15,000 for video, 10:00–22:00, with a surcharge if normal service has to stop.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13022696 gives the address 東京都渋谷区神山町10-8, the coordinates 35.663369/139.694797, the phone 03-3460-0088, the 2006-04-01 opening date, the former name 清山, the weekday 12:00–14:00 / 17:30–21:30 and Saturday 12:00–20:00 hours, the Sunday/holiday closure, the course prices ¥5,500/¥7,700/¥11,000 with a two-person minimum, the note that Saturday takes no bookings and closes when the soba runs out, plus 20 seats, private rooms, all non-smoking, cards/IC/PayPay accepted and a 10% service charge. Hot Pepper strJ001128325 adds the stone-milled domestic buckwheat, the Mt Haruna spring water, the 牛すじ肉の蕎麦湯抜き, the ~50 sake and a lower course tier (¥4,400/¥6,600/¥9,900) — the two price sets disagree, so the Tabelog figures are used and the Hot Pepper ones noted. kamiyama.mystrikingly.com is the shop's studio-rental page and describes the two floors and seat counts. The domain www.soba-kamiyama.com, cited by that page as the restaurant's site, now serves a parked ad page and is not usable as a source, so no website has been recorded.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Soba is cut on a board dusted with 打ち粉 and boiled in shared water; tempura runs on the booked courses. Nothing here is protected from wheat.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tsuyu is a conventional soba-shop dipping sauce; no gluten-free tamari is named anywhere. Assume wheat in every sauce and simmered dish.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi in the tsuyu, egg in the 卵焼き, and the house braise is beef tendon cooked in the soba water itself — the soba-yu poured at the end of the meal is not a neutral liquid here.

positives.text: Evening service is booked-course-only for two or more, so dietary questions can be raised at the time of booking rather than at the door.

All seats non-smoking; cards (VISA/Master/JCB/AMEX/Diners), transport IC and PayPay accepted; free Wi-Fi; private and half-private rooms for 2 and 6. Children of primary-school age and up are accepted with one order each.

cultural_comfort.note: A composed, modern room rather than a tourist door, and it takes a little planning. Lunch (12:00–14:00) is the easy entry: a seiro and a beer, walk-in. Evenings are reservation-only, courses only, two people minimum, with a 10% service charge and a 10% private-room charge on top — so a solo traveller cannot simply turn up after 17:30. No English menu is documented and there is no working shop website (the domain the studio page cites is now a parked ad page), so booking is by phone in Japanese on 03-3460-0088 or through Tabelog's online reservation. Cards, Suica and PayPay all work, and everything is non-smoking. Closed Sundays and public holidays; Saturday is walk-in only and closes when the soba runs out.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Real shop; exact address and coordinates now set from Tabelog (東京都渋谷区神山町10-8, 35.663369/139.694797). name: 福田屋
address_ja: 〒150-0043 東京都渋谷区道玄坂2-25-15 福田ビル 2F
cuisine: A 1952 neighbourhood soba house up a stair off Dōgenzaka: forty seats, greenery through the windows, and a long machi-soba card from のりかけせいろ at ¥1,100 to 天ちらせいろ at ¥2,600 — lunch only now, cash only
neighborhood: Dōgenzaka 2-25-15, in the Dōgenzaka-kōji lane behind the Yamada Denki building — 351 m from Shibuya Station, 3 min from the Keiō Inokashira west exit and from the Hanzōmon / Den-en-toshi exits, 6 min from JR
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金・土 11:00-14:30　日・祝日 定休　※店主がご高齢のため、夜の営業は止めてランチのみになりました
gf_detail: Wheat is structural and there is no gluten-free claim. This is a conventional Tokyo machi-soba: the tsuyu is wheat soy sauce (no tamari named anywhere), the board is dusted with 打ち粉, and the card is built around tempura — 天ちらせいろ ¥2,600, 天せいろ ¥2,000, かき揚げせいろ ¥1,700, カレー南蛮そば ¥1,700, all battered or roux-thickened. Even the plainest せいろ is dipped in wheat. There is nothing here for a celiac.
vegan_detail: The tsuyu is a bonito dashi and it is on every dish, hot and cold; 玉子とじ, 鴨せいろ, とり団子せいろ and 納豆そば run through the card, and the fryer handles prawn, squid and vegetables together. 野菜天せいろ (¥1,700) and the seasonal 冷やしなすそば (¥1,500, April–October) are vegetable dishes on paper, but they are still served with the fish-dashi tsuyu and out of a shared fryer, so they are not vegan.

chef_bio.background: 福田屋 opened in 1952 and has held the same lane in Dōgenzaka ever since, through every rebuild of Shibuya around it — it now sits on the second floor of the Fukuda Building, the family's own block, up a stair off Dōgenzaka-kōji behind Yamada Denki. Forty seats over two-tops, four-tops and one large communal table; windows that look onto greenery, which local write-ups repeatedly call 都会のオアシス, an urban oasis a hundred metres from the Shibuya scramble; all non-smoking, with a smoking spot outside; no cards, no e-money, no QR payment, cash only. What is worth knowing before planning a trip is that the shop has contracted: 「店主がご高齢のため、夜の営業は止めてランチのみになりました」 — the proprietor is elderly, so evening service has been dropped and it now opens only 11:00–14:30, Monday to Saturday. The card is still a full machi-soba card of about seventy-four dishes, priced ¥1,100–¥2,600, and Tabelog's menu page was last updated in May 2026, so it is current. Neither the proprietor's name nor the family line is published on any source that could be opened; no bio has been invented for them.
chef_bio.philosophy: Not stated by the shop. What the sources show is a plain, consistent machi-soba kitchen — the local write-ups keep using the phrase 安定のクォリティ, 'the reliable quality', of a shop that has been doing the same thing since 1952.
chef_bio.specialty: 天ちらせいろ ¥2,600 (two prawns, squid, vegetables); 天せいろ ¥2,000; かき揚げせいろ / かき揚げそば ¥1,700; 鴨せいろ ¥1,700; 冷やしたぬきそば ¥1,300; 巣ごもりそば ¥1,500; seasonal 冷やしなすそば ¥1,500 (April–October).

anecdotes.text: The shop dates itself to 1952 — a local write-up marks it as the year Yoshio Shirai became Japan's first world boxing champion — and it is still in the family building, 福田ビル, that carries its name.
Evening service has been given up because the proprietor is now elderly; the shop runs lunch only, 11:00 to 14:30.
Forty seats with a view of greenery through the windows, three minutes from the Shibuya scramble.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13001915 gives the address 東京都渋谷区道玄坂2-25-15 福田ビル2F, the coordinates 35.659792/139.697628, the phone 03-3476-6437, the 1952 opening year, the 11:00–14:30 Monday–Saturday hours with Sunday and public holidays closed, 40 seats (2×2, 4×7 and a large table), all non-smoking with an outdoor smoking spot, cash only, no private room, no group bookings, and a ¥1,000–¥1,999 budget; its menu page (updated 2026-05-22) carries the full priced card quoted above. gf_cross_contamination.text: Soba and udon come off the same card and the same boil, and the tempura fryer runs through the whole service. Wheat is in the tsuyu regardless.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: A 1952 machi-soba tsuyu — soy sauce, mirin, dashi. No gluten-free tamari is named on the menu or anywhere else, so assume wheat in every bowl and every dipping cup.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi in every tsuyu; duck, chicken-meatball, egg and natto dishes on the same card; prawn and squid through the same fryer as the vegetable tempura.

positives.text: All seats non-smoking (the smoking spot is outside the shop), 40 seats with room to sit rather than a stand-up counter, and a quiet lane rather than the Dōgenzaka crowd.

cultural_comfort.note: An old-Shibuya lunch counter, welcoming but unadapted. Cash only — no cards, no IC, no QR — so bring yen. No English menu is documented and no shop website exists; the card is Japanese, and Tabelog's photographed menu page is the practical way to choose before you go. Open 11:00–14:30 only, Monday to Saturday; closed Sundays and public holidays, and closed every evening since the proprietor stopped running dinner. Forty seats and no group reservations, so at 12:30 on a weekday expect to queue. Second floor, up a stair — not step-free. The compensations are real: three minutes from Shibuya Station, non-smoking, calm, green out of the window, and ¥1,100–¥2,000 will feed you well.

roles: 代表取締役社長, 株式会社 本家つる㐂 (ninth generation)
chef_bio.origin: Sakamoto, Ōtsu, Shiga — at the foot of Mt Hiei
chef_bio.background: The house dates itself to 享保元年 (1716), when a man called 鶴屋喜八 opened a soba shop in the village of Sakamoto below Enryaku-ji; the shop's name is his. Because Enryaku-ji's abbots were imperial princes, the family were called up the mountain to make soba for visitors from the Kyoto Gosho, and the shop still trades on being 延暦寺御用達 and, through that connection, 宮家御用達. The ninth-generation president, 上延昌洋, writes that he learned to cut soba at the same 手打台 that has stood there since 1716, as the eighth-generation chairman did before him and as the tenth-generation cutter does now, and that he does the gift wrapping and the garden sweeping himself at night so that hand-cutting is never squeezed. In 2025 he finished a six-year project to reproduce the shop's soba as a dried noodle for elderly regulars and for children who had moved to Tokyo and could not get home. Two separate companies now carry the 鶴喜 name: 株式会社本家つる㐂 (手打蕎麦 鶴屋喜八), which consolidated its branches and states 「支店統合し、現在は一店舗のみで経営しております」 — one shop only, in Sakamoto; and 鶴喜そば製菓株式会社 at 坂本2-12-33, whose four outlets are Karasaki, Yamashina in Kyoto, and two on Mt Hiei at the Daikōdō and the Warōdō. Neither has a Tokyo shop. An Akasaka branch is remembered in old blog and video material, but it is gone, and no current source places any 鶴喜 in Tokyo. All of this belongs to Shiga, so it has not been written up as a Tokyo bio.
chef_bio.philosophy: 手打の統一 — one shop, so that every noodle is cut by hand on the founding board; three hundred years of the same sweet kaeshi kept in the same pot.
chef_bio.specialty: Nihachi hand-cut soba from domestic buckwheat and domestic wheat; the house sweet kaeshi tsuyu; a dried-noodle gift set launched in 2025.

anecdotes.text: The dried-noodle project began with a customer's letter: elderly parents still living in Sakamoto, children in Tokyo, and no way to hand over Tsuruki's soba on a flying visit a month before New Year — the shop could not sell its hand-cut soba because it does not keep overnight.

For the packaging, the president asked the Shiga calligrapher Shūren to write the two characters 手打 — but first sat her in front of the family's butsudan to hear the three-hundred-year oral history after a reading of the Heart Sutra.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: tsurukisoba.com (株式会社本家つる㐂) gives the address 滋賀県大津市坂本4-11-40, the phone 077-578-0002, the 11:00–16:00 hours and the dated closing days, the president's name 上延昌洋, the 享保元年 founding, the 延暦寺御用達 / 宮家御用達 claim, the nihachi statement 「江戸時代の蕎麦の継承をしているため二八蕎麦です」, and the flat statement that the company consolidated its branches and now runs one shop only. tsurukisoba.co.jp (鶴喜そば製菓株式会社, 坂本2-12-33) is the separate confectionery/restaurant company; its shop guide lists 唐崎店 (大津市唐崎1-23-1), 山科店 (京都市山科区小山北溝町1), 比叡山店 大講堂 and 比叡山店 和労堂 (both 大津市坂本本町4220). Every 鶴喜 soba shop is in Shiga or Kyoto — the hand-cut head shop in Sakamoto, Ōtsu, and the four 鶴喜そば製菓 outlets at Karasaki, Yamashina and on Mt Hiei — roughly 400 km from Aoyama-itchome. name: 恵比寿横丁
address_ja: 〒150-0013 東京都渋谷区恵比寿1-7-4 第一協栄ビル1F
cuisine: Not one restaurant but a covered alley of about nineteen tiny counters under red lanterns — charcoal grill, Kyoto-style oden, kushiage, horse- and beef-nigiri, a mushroom specialist, a small bistro — where you drink at one and move to the next, most of them open from late afternoon until around 3 a.m.
neighborhood: Ebisu 1-7-4, a short covered arcade off the street outside Ebisu Station's west exit — 187 m from JR Ebisu (Yamanote / Saikyō), 2–3 min on foot, 3 min from the Hibiya line
hours_raw: 店舗により異なる（多くは夕方～翌3時頃、不定休）。「忘れ物・予約・営業時間については各店に直接お問い合わせ下さい」／「こちら営業時間は、予告無しに変更される場合もございます」
gf_detail: Nineteen independent counters, not one of which publishes an allergen statement, and the food is wheat from end to end: 串揚げ ぶるどっく deep-fries in panko breadcrumbs; でんらく is 京風おでん, whose broth is soy sauce and whose 竹輪 and 薩摩揚げ commonly carry wheat starch; 純ちゃん is a Hakata izakaya; there are teppanyaki, hormone-teppan and pork-yakiniku counters whose tare is soy-based; and every one of them seasons with ordinary wheat soy sauce. The stalls are open-fronted along a single narrow lane, with grills and a fryer running side by side. Nothing here can be made safe for a celiac, and there is no one at a venue level to ask — each shop is its own operator.
vegan_detail: No shop in the alley publishes a vegan option, and the published genres are meat- and fish-led: charcoal grill, meat sushi, pork yakiniku, hormone teppan, hamayaki shellfish, sashimi and robatayaki. Two of the nineteen at least point in a plant direction — きのこ料理きのこ, a mushroom-cuisine counter, and a wine-and-vegetables stall — but a Japanese izakaya's vegetable plates are still seasoned with wheat soy sauce and finished with bonito dashi or katsuobushi as a matter of course, and none of these kitchens says otherwise. Treat it as something to ask about at the individual counter, in Japanese, before ordering; the alley's whole premise of grazing across several shops makes it hard to hold a line.

roles: creator / producer of 恵比寿横丁
founder, 株式会社浜倉的商店製作所 (Hamakura-teki Shōten Seisakusho)
chef_bio.origin: Ebisu, Shibuya-ku — the site of the former 山下ショッピングセンター
chef_bio.background: 恵比寿横丁 is a made thing, and knowing that makes it easier to read. The site was a public market called 山下ショッピングセンター; as Ebisu Station was redeveloped through the 2000s, that one corner was left behind and shuttered, with a single fish seller still trading when 浜倉好宣 found it. He opened the alley in 2008 with thirteen counters — the number has since grown to around nineteen or twenty — under the banner of what his company calls ほっこり横丁, a 'cosy alley' where a teenager and a retiree can end up drinking at the same plank. Hamakura, born June 1967, went on to build a whole genre of these revived-market drinking halls through 株式会社浜倉的商店製作所, and 恵比寿横丁 is the one that made his name. The individual counters are separately run and separately named — 炭火焼 まるや, でんらく (京風おでん), 浜椿 (紹興酒家), 純ちゃん (博多居酒屋), 串揚げ ぶるどっく, 魚〇 (浜焼き酒場), 銀〇 (ホイル焼き酒場), 牛〇 (牛酒場), 貝〇 (刺身・炉端焼き), 豚焼セレブ にん肉, 達磨天狗 (ホルモン鉄板), 肉寿司, 魚串, Bistro maman, うめ月 (鉄板焼き), きのこ料理きのこ, 馬ルタン羊人 (馬肉・生ラム), 高橋さん and 姫島 — so there is no single chef and none is claimed here.
chef_bio.philosophy: ほっこり横丁 — reviving a dead market street as a place where strangers of every age drink elbow to elbow. The venue's own line for the project is 「かつて慣れ親しんだ『山下ショッピングセンター』。商店街として栄えていた通り道にふたたび人が集まり、楽しいこと、おもしろいこと、あの時の時間がよみがえる」.
chef_bio.specialty: Alley-hopping across nineteen counters: charcoal-grilled skewers, Kyoto-style oden, kushiage, horse- and beef-nigiri at 肉寿司, hamayaki shellfish, teppanyaki, mushroom cookery and a small bistro — most of them serving until around 3 a.m.

anecdotes.text: When Hamakura found the site, the 山下ショッピングセンター was a public market that had emptied out as the rest of Ebisu was rebuilt around it — one fishmonger was still trading among the shutters. 「オープンしたのは2008年。もともと『山下ショッピングセンター』という公設市場だった。」
It opened with thirteen counters inside a forty-year-old shell, and the format — an artificial yokocho built into a dead shopping street — became a template Hamakura's company repeated across Tokyo.

The alley's own house rules are refreshingly blunt: bookings, lost property and opening hours are the individual shops' business, not the yokocho's — 「忘れ物・予約・営業時間については各店に直接お問い合わせ下さい」 — and most, but not all, of them will do takeaway.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: ebisu-yokocho.com is the official site: its shop directory lists the counters by number, name, genre and phone (19 entries, from 炭火焼 まるや to 馬ルタン羊人 and 姫島) with a per-shop opening-hours grid, and states that hours change without notice and that reservations must be made with each shop directly. gotokyo.org (Tokyo's official tourism site) gives the address 東京都渋谷区恵比寿1-7-4 and 'JR Ebisu, 2 min'. The Yahoo News Japan long-form feature on 浜倉好宣 dates the opening to 2008 and identifies the site as the former 公設市場 山下ショッピングセンター, left stranded by the 2000s redevelopment of Ebisu Station. in-shoku.info's profile gives Hamakura's birth month (June 1967), the thirteen-shop original format, the forty-year-old building and the ほっこり横丁 concept — though it dates the opening to 2010 and names the predecessor building differently, so the Yahoo News / official-site version has been preferred. Tabelog 13109981 (恵比寿横丁 肉寿司) confirms the building as 第一協栄ビル1F, gives the coordinates 35.648107/139.710696, 187 m from Ebisu Station, 16:00–03:00, no reservations, 不定休.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A single narrow covered lane of open-fronted counters: a panko deep-fryer (串揚げ ぶるどっく), charcoal grills, teppan plates and an oden pot all within a few metres of each other. Shared surfaces and airborne flour are unavoidable, and no shop publishes an allergen policy.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Every genre in the alley is soy-sauce-seasoned — Kyoto-style oden broth, yakiniku and hormone tare, robata, hamayaki. No gluten-free tamari is named by any of the nineteen shops.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Grills and plates are shared between meat, fish and vegetables at every counter; the two plant-leaning stalls (きのこ料理きのこ and the wine-and-vegetables counter) sit in the same lane and publish nothing about dashi or katsuobushi.

positives.text: Every shop's phone number is published on the official directory, so a Japanese-speaking friend or hotel concierge can ring one specific counter ahead rather than negotiating in the crowd.
Ground level and step-free from the street, 187 m from Ebisu Station, and open until roughly 3 a.m. — a workable late option when kitchens elsewhere have closed.

cultural_comfort.level: Lively — easy to enter, hard to control
cultural_comfort.note: One of the friendliest doors in Tokyo and one of the worst rooms for anyone managing a diet. The alley is open to the street, step-free, two minutes from Ebisu Station, visibly full of foreign visitors, and nobody minds a stranger sitting down; several counters take cards and the 肉寿司 stall runs 16:00–03:00 with no bookings. But the seats are shoulder-to-shoulder plank benches, it is loud, it is smoky from charcoal, and the whole premise is grazing across several kitchens in one night — which means having the allergy conversation four or five times, in Japanese, standing up, in a crowd, with nineteen separate operators who share no policy. If someone in the party is celiac, treat this as a place to have a drink rather than to eat. Hours vary by shop and change without notice; the official directory carries each counter's own phone number and hours grid.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED, with a CATEGORY FLAG. 恵比寿横丁 exists and the address and coordinates are now exact (東京都渋谷区恵比寿1-7-4 第一協栄ビル1F, 35.648107/139.710696, taken from the Tabelog listing of 恵比寿横丁 肉寿司 inside it). But it is not a MOM_AND_POP restaurant — it is a 2008-built covered alley of about nineteen independently run counters, produced by 浜倉好宣 of 浜倉的商店製作所 on the site of the derelict 山下ショッピングセンター public market. Suggest recategorising as a venue / food-alley entry, and note that hours, reservations and payment differ per shop. gf downgraded from the sweep's 'ask' to 'no' (panko fryer, oden, soy-based tare, no allergen policy at any of the nineteen); vegan set to 'ask' rather than the sweep's 'limited' — two counters lean plant-ward but none publishes a dashi-free claim. Sources disagree on the opening year (Yahoo News and the official site support 2008; one trade profile says 2010) — 2008 used.
